title: The estimate opens as a wedge

members.role: the page lands on its axes and the ACTUAL line draws (the 2025 datum on its own word at +7.44); the two estimate edges are held at 2025 by a build_to at index 0
on the projection's word ('This year') both estimate edges draw out of the last actual datum over 1.2 s - the projection opens from the real line, never from nowhere
the wedge between the high edge and the low edge bleeds full of ink - the range is an AREA between two lines, never a midpoint line (E53, E77)
the hand writes the RANGE as the figure - '$130–150B' over '2026E' - at the high edge's end, never one number

does: A line lands on its actuals; on the projection's word two estimate edges draw out of the last real datum, the wedge between them fills with ink, and the hand writes the range as the figure - an estimate is a range, never a midpoint.

use_when.act: COMPARES over time - a PROJECTION (SPECIES-BY-SENTENCE has no projecting act; BRAVOS-USE-WHEN 3b)
use_when.shape: a series of actuals + a RANGE for the next point (two estimate edges out of the last actual)
use_when.use: a sentence that projects a figure its sources give as a range ('tracking toward', 'on track to', '2026E'): the actuals land first, the wedge opens on the projection's word, the range is written
use_when.dont: a single-point forecast (continue the line dashed), a range with no actual to open from, or the midpoint written as the number (E53, E77)

source: P69 T35 (the operator 2026-09-22); proved as a beat by projects/_proofs/p69-recipes/proof_p69_recipes.py on Steel and Paper H row 16 ('Between 2020 and 2024 ... toward a hundred and fifty', take 256.48 s) on ev-debt-issuance-line-v1 - no approved cut carries it
